recipes.name: Carla's Sausage Cheese Balls
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package bulk mild pork sausage
1 (16 ounce) package bulk hot pork sausage
1 (8 ounce) package shredded sharp Cheddar cheese
2 cups biscuit baking mix (such as Bisquick®)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Mix mild sausage and hot sausage in a large bowl until evenly blended.
Stir Cheddar cheese into sausage mixture.
Mix biscuit baking mix into sausage mixture about 1/2 cup at a time until baking mix is moist.
Roll meat mixture into 1 1/4- to 1 1/2-inch balls.
Arrange meatballs on prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until meatballs are no longer pink in the center and cheese is browned, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Carla's Sausage Cheese Balls

review.reviewBody: I made these for my husband's office for breakfast. Very simple ingredients - just make sure it is well incorporated before rolling into balls. It will look very dry and crumbly, but, keep working with it and it will come together into a smooth ball. Make sure you don't see any of the dry Bisquick. I only used about 1-1/2 lbs of sausage and about 1-1/2 cups of Bisquick. My oven cooks hot - so, I also baked at 350 for 20 minutes instead of 400 and they were perfect. I also baked them on a parchment covered baking sheet and they came right off the paper. Thanks, Mitchell!
I have found that if I microwave the sausage for a bit, it is easier to mix with the other ingredients. After cooling, I freeze these in a ziplock bag and microwave as many as needed for breakfast.

I used hot and mild sausages, 8 oz of sharp cheddar cheese, 4 oz of cream cheese, 1.5 cup of pancake mix, and made 45 balls. I froze the balls before baking , and baked them in 350 degrees for 25 minutes. They came out moist and tasty. Also I used silicone baking mat so they easily came off. Next time I will put sliced jalapeno and onion.

I've been making these for years. I use the Bob Evans Zesty style pork sausage for mine. Really gives it a nice kick without bing too hot. I always add more cheese because well, CHEESE!! I add 2 tsp. baking powder as well. This really makes them puff up. I also use 1/2 Cup of water, otherwise they're a little dry. One more thing I'd like to add is that I grate my own cheese. When you buy the pre-grated cheese they put some drying chemicals on it so the cheese won't stick together. That dries out the sausage balls. Just grate your own, you'll not be sorry you did. These sausage balls are SO much better when you do it yourself.
Delicious! I used Jimmy Deans sausage, did NOT precook it before baking, baked at 350 bc my oven cooks hot. These were a HUGE hit at a church breakfast. I will make these again!

First time I followed the directions however I had to substitute flour, baking powder, salt and butter for bisquick since I didn’t have any. Turned out great. Cook time ended up around 12 min. Next time added more sharp cheddar and added crushed red pepper. Much more robust and memorable with the added items. Third time accidentally added double the cheese along with the other changes. This is now my go to cheese ball recipe. With my changes.

FYI - It says makes 12 servings, and my batch made 60 1-1.5" balls. So I guess it's 5 balls = 1 serving?

The sausage I used was 1 lb Great Value brand mild pork sausage (in the chub) + 4 links (about .8 lbs) of Great Value mild Italian pork sausage. I didn't have sharp cheddar, so I used medium cheddar (Tillamook) and grated a little over half of my full pound brick. (a little extra cheese to make up for the too little sausage). A full 2 cups of regular bisquick. It made 62 balls for me. Baked at 400 for 17 minutes on parchment paper lined pans. These produce a fair amount of oil/grease, so best to use a fully rimmed pan to prevent spills when taking out of the oven. 

The flavor was great, though mild. Perfect for the kid and parent crowd at my party tomorrow, though sophisticated palettes will appreciate using the hot sausage and sharp cheddar IMHO.

Vegetarian option:
I know it sounds weird making sausage balls vegetarian but I use Light Life Gimme Lean ground sausage and it works very well. I don't use vegan cheese because I feel that stuff is not very good but I do use Cabot farms cheese and it's a rennet free cheese so it just has the dairy as the only animal product. They will seem a little dry but just work them into balls and when the cheese melts they will be moist. I take these to work and the non vegetarian people have no idea their meat free.

I've been making these for years. I use all hot sausage (we love spicy!) and I also add a couple dashes of garlic powder over the sausage before mixing it all up with my hands. Oh! And I grate my own sharp cheddar, also. Makes a big difference!

After I mixed all and put balls on cookie sheets I put in the Refrigerator? for 20 minutes then cooked in preheated oven for 10 minutes turned over the sausage balls and cooked another 10 minutes. Turned out great and everybody loved them!
Love this recipe and have made multiple times. We use 1 package of sage sausage and one of hot. And we just about double the cheese. A favorite at our house!
Just the right ratio of sausage and bisquick...delicious!!!!
I use this recipe as a base when I make sausage balls. I use more sausage and cheese in mine just because I like mine meatier and cheesier. It's a great recipe. Sausage balls are my favorites.
I tried to cut the recipe in half but it needed more bisquick. Came out more of a meatball than breaded cheese ball. Delicious nonetheless!
My husband loves these, they remind him of the ones she use to make around the holidays. To honor her memory I add buttermilk to match her recipe.
Easy to make and delicious
Love these for Christmas morning. Tip: Mix sausage and Bisquick first, then add cheese. SO much easier.
I forgot how much I love these! Since my daughter prefers ground turkey, we used Jennie-O Italian Style ground turkey and added red pepper flakes and creole seasoning. Delicious!
Added 1/2 a chopped onion , big hit at the party, very good!
This was very easy to make I think the hardest part was making sure everything was mixed well. But it turned out well.
